note: Rule register. Every rule is re-run by tools/probe.py (and by tools/validate.py --tests). outcome: CONFIRMED = discriminating evidence for the statement; CONSISTENT_NOT_DISCRIMINATED = everything matched so far is compatible, but no experiment has yet shown the alternative fails; FALSIFIED = evidence against.

rules.statement: All three episodes were linked with the Turbo C 2.0 large-model startup: C0L.OBJ _TEXT equals image bytes [0,455) outside its own fixups in DN1/DN2/DN3; C0S/C0T/C0C/C0M/C0H all differ.

TASM 1.0 (/D__LARGE__ /MX) reassembles the shipped STARTUP\C0.ASM to the same _TEXT bytes, fixups and publics as the shipped C0L.OBJ, so a C0 variant with appended assembly (the region [0x1C9,0x603) shared by all episodes) is buildable from source with the pinned assembler. The game's own C0 variant is NOT yet reconstructed.

65 Turbo C 2.0 CL.LIB code segments (12,849 bytes) are located in each episode: 64 by a unique exact match outside fixups, plus the 4-byte REALCVT _TEXT placed positionally in the only gap it fills; the remaining 2/3/5 zero bytes are TLINK fill before the paragraph-aligned DELAY_TEXT. Library code is CL.LIB (large model).

LZEXE 0.91 stores relocations as ascending deltas with paragraph-normalised offsets, so the original TLINK relocation table order and seg:off split are not recoverable from DN?.EXE; acceptance compares relocation sets only.
-O (jump optimisation) is in effect for G1/G2 C code: without it the canonical pilots grow jump chains (jmp $+2) and stop matching.
-K (char is unsigned) is in effect: without it char loads gain cbw and compares widen.
-G (optimise for speed) is in effect: 2-byte caller cleanup is 'inc sp; inc sp' instead of 'pop cx'.
-1- (8086 instructions) is in effect: with -1 (80186) 'push imm' replaces 'mov ax,imm; push ax' and g1_006f stops matching.
-Z (register load suppression) is in effect: removing it makes 68 of 170 accepted C functions stop matching (scan of 2026-10-13); the rule re-checks a fixed sample.
Object-level: with -Z, 'a = b; c = b;' stores AX twice without reloading b; without -Z it reloads. Pattern to look for when hunting a -Z discriminator in the original code.

Large model, one translation unit: calls to externals are relocated far calls (EXTDEF fixup); calls to functions defined earlier, and to static functions even when only forward-declared, are 'push cs; call near' resolved at compile time (no fixup); calls to public functions defined later are far calls with an own-segment fixup. Consequence (tools/tu.py, evidence/tu-structure.json): in the originals, backward far calls inside one segment never occur (0 in G1 and G2 in every episode), consistent with one translation unit per segment; there are also 0 forward 'push cs; call near', so no static function is evidenced yet (an earlier raw byte-pattern count of 197 was a false positive).
Functions ending in 'retf N' are pascal: g1_e92e matches only when declared pascal (callers then do no stack cleanup, cf. g1_006f calling g2_1f5a).

The pinned TLINK 2.0 links a large-model unit with C0L.OBJ and CL.LIB under the pinned runner (/c /d /s), and the far library segments pulled in by the startup's own references come out in the same order as the first library segments of the originals (IOERROR, EXIT, ATEXIT, FMALLOC, FBRK, SETBLOCK).

The pinned LZEXE 0.91 (bellard.org/lzexe/lzexe91.zip) run headless in DOSBox-X turns the canonical unpacked image of each episode back into the byte-identical original DN?.EXE. Packed-file equality therefore follows from unpacked-image equality (image bytes, relocation set, header fields); the TLINK relocation order is irrelevant because LZEXE sorts relocations.

Object level (probes/data_layout.c): a unit's _DATA holds its initialised globals first, in definition order (explicit zero initialisers included), then every string literal of the unit in order of appearance; duplicates are kept unless -d is given. Uninitialised globals go to _BSS (static ones not in plain definition order: open).

In every episode G2's literal references are all distinct offsets while the referenced texts repeat (e.g. the same 'Press any key.' line), so G2 was compiled without -d (string merging), consistent with the default profile.

Turbo C 2.0 assigns SI to the `register` variable (local or parameter) with the highest weighted use count and DI to the next; each use counts 3x per enclosing for/while/do loop (label/goto loops are not weighted); ties keep declaration order. Declaration order alone does not decide (g1_af06, g1_3a98: label loops give the outer counter SI).

With -O, Turbo C 2.0 cross-jumps identical instruction tails of different branches: the matching suffix is emitted once and the other branch jumps into it. Duplicated code in the original therefore means the two tails differ somewhere; shared code can come from two identical source tails (g1_fd15).

In a function with a BP frame but no locals and no saved SI/DI, Turbo C 2.0 follows every cdecl call, even one without arguments, with `mov sp,bp`; pascal calls get no cleanup. A zero-argument callee called without that cleanup from such a caller is pascal (g1_ec3d, g1_fd15, g1_fc85 from main; g1_1b51, g1_2a1d, g1_bb9f from g1_e3e0).
